sentences.text: Aisha Bello is a mental health social worker from the community mental health team.
Callum Reid is the person being assessed.
Dr Shah, Callum's GP, requested the community mental health team to visit Callum.
Callum's mother informed the social worker that she was at work when the visit occurred.
Callum has been feeling low since about the summer.
Callum dropped out of college in September.
Callum was studying engineering at Level three.
Callum has been sleeping badly, staying awake until 4 or 5 a.m. and sleeping during the day.
Callum has been eating little, mainly consuming toast, and has not eaten much otherwise.
Callum has asthma and uses an inhaler.
Callum was previously employed at a warehouse during Christmas as a temporary worker last year.
Callum currently has no employment or income.
Callum's mother is a nurse who works night shifts and is currently at work during the visit.
Callum's mother is aware that he is feeling down, but not aware of the full extent of his emotional state.
Callum has limited social contact; he only speaks to his friend Josh online and his sister, who is at university in Leeds.
Callum's dog, Bailey, is a staffy (a mix of staffordshire terrier), three years old, and sleeps on Callum's bed.
Callum does not currently have any tablets stored in his flat, only having paracetamol left by his mother in the kitchen.
Callum is currently feeling okay today and does not intend to do anything harmful today.
Callum has self-harmed by cutting his arms, which has occurred most nights for about two months.
The self-harm is not deep and has not required stitches or medical treatment for infection.
Callum has not taken an overdose of tablets or any medication.
Callum has thought about ending his life, specifically stating he wanted to die 'properly' in the last few weeks.
Callum went for a walk to Calder Bridge last week and considered jumping off the bridge.
Callum was stopped from jumping off the bridge by his mother and his dog, Bailey.
The crisis team will visit Callum at home tomorrow to assess his situation.
The crisis team visit will be arranged by the social worker, who will contact Callum directly to confirm the visit.
The social worker will contact Callum's mother at 6 p.m. that evening to inform her of Callum's situation.
Callum's mother will be asked to keep the paracetamol locked away for now.
The practice nurse from Dr Shah's practice will examine Callum's arms on Thursday, the 26th.
The social worker will return to visit Callum on Monday, the 30th.
